Kate Kruckemeyer asked if anyone for the proposed zone change can come forward, Ryan Rippa came forward and introduced himself. Ryan explained the zone change and he is looking to develop this property into a residential reuse and it would be a mill building with an office in the middle, and then an industrial part on the side with a 120-bed residential treatment facility attached. Ryan described all services for clients would be held on site with no impacted traffic and ample parking and mentioned the existing zone it is currently in does not allow for this use and that is why he proposed the zone change to DR.

Jeffery Burkott discussed the zoning proposal cannot be rezoned to DR due to its location surrounded by IR and BH zones, also the challenges and limitations regarding the proposed reuse of a property for a specific intended use due to structural and proximity constraints.

The Board agreed on the decision to deny the zone change request for 12 Crescent Street from IG to DR, citing concerns about spot zoning.

## PLANNING BOARD BUSINESS

1.) **Project Updates/Old Business/New Business:**

a.) Comprehensive Plan update; final Plan presentation, Agency Landscape + Planning

Allen Penniman began the discussion by displaying a slideshow of the Comprehensive Plan, Allen discussed the four themes which are livability, business ecosystem, sustainability, and community safety for Holyoke's future land use framework, focusing on making the city livable and welcoming, and supporting business development. He discussed the implementation pathways for Holyoke's comprehensive plan, outlining both internal and external actions needed to bring the plan to life and explained that it took two and a half years to develop due to leadership transitions. Kate Kruckemeyer provided context on the plan's necessity and outlined next steps, including the planning board's vote to approve it, she then asked if anyone from the public had any comments or questions, Christine Fuita came forward and asked the Mayor Joshua Garcia, "what happened to the roadshow for the comp plan around through the community and enable the community to respond to it, potentially modify it based on the community's feedback?" Mayor Joshua Garcia replied "we did bring on board some support and capacity to help us do community citywide engagement it was an extensive process in trying to review who can help best do that work, but Eric Nakajima is here, I believe. As soon as this week or next week, people will start hearing some outreach, and really what we want to do is try to get City Hall into the neighborhoods, and the comprehensive plan is going to be the focal point of all that, because it really covers a lot you know, we have a community. Diversity is always great, but community engagement can be vastly difficult from West Holyoke to South Holyoke, considering, the differences of perspectives and personalities, and the cultures are different."

After the Mayor spoke, Theresa Cooper-Gordon came forward and discussed her concerns with public safety and not enough police officers are patrolling the areas in Holyoke where officers are needed most and for the community to get involved, they need to feel safety first.

Councilor Linda Vacon then joined the discussion and stated to the Board and Allen in one of the documents, an executive committee was listed as having worked along with the planning board for the 24 months, then asked who the executive committee was. Allen and Kate stated that information is on the city's website on the 15th page of the Comprehensive Plan and it is on the left side column and is labeled the Comprehensive Plan Committee.

Councilor Richard Purcell came forward and introduced himself, he explained to the Board that Ward 1 and Ward 2 are the wards that suffer the most and asked the Board to consider those two Wards when making decisions on the Comprehensive Plan and consider environmental justice, social justice, and economic justice when tip retains to those Wards.

Hazel Alvarez introduced herself, stated she is in Ward 1, and asked the Board where the people in her Ward will be placed, and are they being pushed out where they live and go to school, for this Comprehensive Plan. Kate Kruckemeyer replied that's not any intention of the planning board, and that's not a decision that comes before the Planning Board, and that is what the mayor is trying to roll out in terms of input, bringing that out to the communities for discussion, should be a helpful place. Mayor Joshua Garcia stated the city's intention is to never support or do things to displace people, and supporting the network that's already here, but also making space so that as people's lives improve, they don't feel like they have to leave our city there's opportunities for them.

Theresa Cooper-Gordon came back up to the microphone and gave the idea having "No Loitering" signs and have police officers say to anyone who is loitering that they cannot stay in that spot.

Kate Kruckemeyer gave her input on Hazel Alvarez concerns and stated that the Board really does encourage people from the neighborhoods to come when they see something on our agenda that affects their neighborhood to come. are interested in hearing feedback from people when we take something up like that. Kate made the point to say that's in the plan about, rezoning to more local business in the lower wards along Main Street is really a strategy to try to make those, make the business strip in and through those neighborhoods more amenable to the local community, and not just be a drive-through area.

Paola Ferriera came forward and stated "I want to say I'm extremely concerned about voting on this plan next week. Because, and I'm confused, if the plan I mean, we vote on something to make it official. So, the moment it's official, I don't quite understand how it remains fluid. But also, I was surprised, as I looked at the plan and read the plan, it feels to me like it's a plan that could be or any distressed city in the Commonwealth. And I feel a lack of specificity. And again, I look at, The advisor is a usual 120 usual suspect, and when we go back, how many people were reached, it comes to 1.5% of the population. I'm hearing the consultant explaining the plan, and one of the things that came to mind to me is, great, a bike trail to Springfield, sounds great. But how many people who choose not to have a car, or people who cannot afford a car, are in the physical condition of taking a bicycle and going to Springfield? So, I feel the plan Encompasses a lot of very good sale pitch. I don't feel it encompasses the voice of the community, and is not, at this point, encompasses, like, concrete solution. That would make things better. I love Teresa's comment about signage that could help officers enforce specific things. There's a great lack of specificity for this document that will go to a vote next week."

Christine Fuita asked Allen Penniman if the Conservation Overlay District covering Elmwood Forest, Allen addressed the two maps, and he was unaware they addressed the conservation overlay district in that area and if Christine needed more information on that it was going to be in the Open Space and Recreation Plan.

b.) ISO, File# 170, NOD #9, 6-mos update (VHB letter)

Jeffery Burkott explained the VHB letter and the changes the project has made, such as demolition has begun, the applicant has done the abatement, the applicant anticipates they will have a building permit by the first week of September and they have a target for occupancy for March 2028. The Board agreed to have the applicant come back March 23, 2027 for a 6 month update.
